 Camp Flog Gnaw 2026: What fans need to know about set times, parking and more 
 Here's how to navigate the two-day festival

 Camp Flog Gnaw returns to Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles on Saturday, Nov. 14, and Sunday, Nov. 15.
(File photo by Drew A. Kelley, Press-Telegram/SCNG)
 By Holly Alvarado | halvarado@scng.com PUBLISHED: November 13, 2026 at 9:17 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The carnival is rolling back into Dodger Stadium, and Tyler, the Creator is bringing more than 40 artists along for the ride.
 Camp Flog Gnaw returns to Los Angeles on Saturday, Nov. 14, and Sunday, Nov. 15, converting the stadium grounds into a two-day playground of hip-hop, R&B, rock, carnival rides, games and more.
 Produced in collaboration with Goldenvoice, the annual festival celebrates its 12th edition with a genre-spanning lineup. This year’s performers include Tyler, the Creator, Future, Don Toliver, Steve Lacy, Turnstile , Vince Staples and Leon Thomas.
 Whether you’re heading to the festival to catch your favorite artists, explore the carnival attractions or tune in from home, here’s what fans should know before the weekend.
 Lineup and set times
 Tyler, the Creator will perform Saturday on the Camp stage from 7:50 p.m. to 8:50 p.m., followed by Don Toliver, who will close out the evening from 9:45 to 10:55 p.m. Turnstile is scheduled to perform from 6 p.m. to 7 p.m.
 Other Saturday performers include Vince Staples, JID, Leon Thomas, Lola Young, Wallows, Audrey Nuna, 2hollis, Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE, and Wyatt Waddell.
 On Sunday, Steve Lacy will perform from 7:55 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. on the Camp stage, followed by Future, who will close out the festival from 9:55 p.m. to 10:55 p.m.
 Sunday’s lineup also includes Thee Sacred Souls , Syd, Magdalena Bay, Lupe Fiasco, Isaiah Rashad, Latin Mafia, Quadeca and The Alchemist & Friends.
 Festival gates open at noon both days, with performances spread across three stages: Camp, Flog and Gnaw. Several sets will overlap throughout the weekend. Fans can view the complete schedule at campfloggnaw.com/set-times. 
 Food and festival experiences
 Beyond the music, Flog brings its signature carnival atmosphere to Dodger Stadium with amusement rides, games, exclusive merchandise and a food lineup featuring restaurants from across Southern California and beyond.
 This year’s offerings include Kogi, Tacos 1986, Villa’s Tacos, Dave’s Hot Chicken, Prince St. Pizza, The Boiling Crab, Sandoitchi, Shrimp Daddy, Churrería El Moro, Cena Vegan, Lotus of Siam, Tail O’ the Pup and McConnell’s Fine Ice Creams, among others.
 The lineup also features artist collaborations, including Earl Sweatshirt teaming up with Bludso’s BBQ for South African-inspired peri-peri wings, and Pusha T and Pharrell Williams’ Grindin Coffee joining forces with Noun Coffee.
 Carnival rides are included with festival admission, while games require separate tickets for general admission and VIP attendees. The festival is cashless, accepting major credit cards and contactless payments, including Apple Pay and Google Wallet. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options will also be available.
 Parking and transportation
 Festivalgoers planning to drive should prepare for limited parking, as official festival parking passes are sold out. Parking lots open at 9 a.m. both days, and overnight parking, RVs, tailgating, camping and reentry are prohibited.
 A free round-trip shuttle will operate between Union Station and Dodger Stadium throughout the weekend. Boarding begins at 9 a.m. both days, with the first buses departing around 9:30 a.m. Shuttles will run approximately every 15 to 20 minutes, dropping attendees off at Lot 13 on Stadium Way. The final return shuttle will depart around midnight each night.
 Fans using public transportation can take Metro’s A, B, D or J lines to Union Station before transferring to the free shuttle. Metro riders should also be aware that buses will replace A Line trains between the San Pedro and Florence stations.
 Rideshare and friends-and-family drop-offs will be available at Lot 13 beginning at 10 a.m. Friends-and-family pickups will take place on Sunset Boulevard at Vin Scully Avenue.
 What you can bring
 Clear bags measuring up to 12 inches by 6 inches by 12 inches are permitted. Attendees are encouraged to review the festival’s official bag policy before arriving. Festivalgoers may also bring empty plastic water bottles of 64 ounces or less, non-aerosol sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, handheld fans, parasols, portable phone chargers and blankets or towels measuring no more than 50 by 70 inches.
 Nonprofessional digital cameras, disposable cameras, Polaroids and film cameras are allowed. Prescription medications are also permitted, provided the name on the medication matches the attendee’s government-issued identification.
 Professional cameras with detachable lenses, outside food and beverages, glass or metal bottles, aerosol products and weapons are prohibited.
 How to watch the livestream
 Fans who can’t attend in person can still catch the weekend’s performances through Amazon Music, which returns as the exclusive livestream destination for Camp Flog Gnaw for the fourth consecutive year. The free global broadcast will be available through the Amazon Music app, Twitch, Prime Video and Amazon Live, with no subscription required.
 Hosts Wayno and Jillian Superstar will take viewers behind the scenes with artist interviews and live coverage of the festival’s performances and festivities.
 International rebroadcasts will also be available beginning at 8 a.m. GMT on Nov. 15 and 16, giving viewers across different time zones another opportunity to watch.
 Fans can tune in at music.amazon.com/live/events .
 Camp Flog Gnaw 2026
 When : Noon to 11 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, and Sunday, Nov. 15.
 Where : Dodger Stadium, 1000 Vin Scully Ave., Los Angeles.
 Tickets : The festival is sold out. Fans can check official resale options and the festival waitlist at campfloggnaw.com.
